about: How the entry readers (daodan/core/entries.py) read the syntax tree: the framework's knowledge as data, keyed by grammar of tree-sitter-language-pack (flows spec, principle 2 and point 5.9). `grammars` names the grammar of a language the snapshot reads without tree-sitter. In `queries` one query per grammar, as lines, the forms of a binding each a pattern of its own (in an alternation nested in another, tree-sitter loses matches); a string names the grammar whose query it shares, and `code` the grammar of the expressions written as text in the markup. Captures: @tag and @element, a tag and its element; @event, the attribute as written (several nodes, from the first to the last); @handler, a name that binds when it names a function of the project; @inline, a function written in place as the handler, which binds each function of the project it calls as the snapshot resolved the call; @called, what the event calls, a candidate also when it does not resolve; @code, an expression written as text, read with the `code` grammar; @name, @hint, @text and @computed, the parts of the label; @key, the literal key of a translation call. A capture starting with _ serves a predicate; @method, the method of `this` a handler names. @owner and @prop, the object and the property of a handler written `props.onSave`: a binding only where the object is the props of the component the attribute is in (`bindings`), which a component's parent joins to its own handler. In `strings`, by grammar, the query that reads a string literal (`entries._string`): @text, the content of a literal with no interpolation and no escape, @template, a template, whose text between the backticks is its value with its `${...}` kept for the reader to accept or refuse; the arguments of the calls a rule reads (`flows.py`) are literals only through it. In `calls`, by grammar, how a call labels the control it creates or binds: `label`, the keywords that carry a label; `positional`, whether the first literal by position labels the control a call creates; `setters`, the methods that set it later. In `decorators`, one query per grammar for the decorators and annotations of a function or method, each read from the file's tree (the snapshot keeps them only as folded text): @decorator, one decorator, and @definition, the function it decorates; @name, a decorator's name as written; @argument, beside its @name, the text of a first argument that is a text literal. In `noir`, the entry kind each protocol of OWASP Noir's endpoints is; another protocol stays a shape to classify. In `typegen_blocks`, by grammar, the query that finds every checked file of that generated file by its import (@block, @import), whatever type of config checks it: the blocks `typegen` does not read are gaps. In `typegen`, by grammar, the query that reads the file a framework's own tool generates (`next typegen`: `.next/types/validator.ts`), one block per checked file: @shape, the type of config the tool checks it against, @route, the route that type is written for, and @import, the file it imports, relative to the folder of the generated file. In `next`, for each of those config types, its entry kind and the exports of the file that start it: `exports` (a page: its default export) or `methods` (a route handler: one entry per exported method); another type stays a shape to classify. In `react-router`, the same for the routes `react-router routes --json` and `remix routes --json` print (`entry_points/react_router.py`), by shape: the tool gives each route its `path`, its `index` and its `file`, so a route with a `path` is a `route`, one with `index` an `index`, and one with neither (a layout, the root) a `layout`; its `exports` are the ones of the route module that React Router calls to answer a request: `default` renders the page, `loader` and `action` (and their `client` forms) answer a data request, so a route module with no `default` is a resource route. The other exports (`ErrorBoundary`, `HydrateFallback`, `meta`, `links`, `headers`, `handle`, `shouldRevalidate`) answer no request and are not listed. In `sveltekit`, by the name of the file as `svelte-kit sync` lists it (`+server`, `+page.server`, `+page`, `+layout.server`, `+layout`; `entry_points/sveltekit.py`), its entry kind and the `exports` of that file that SvelteKit calls: the methods of a `+server` (`fallback` answers the others), `load` of a page's modules, `load` and the form `actions` of a `+page.server`; a layout's `load` runs for every page under it and starts no flow of its own here. In `declared`, by grammar, what the declaration an index gives an attribute means (`occurrences` of the edge view, the type checker's answer at the attribute): `elements`, by package, the suffixes of the declaring types that are an element's own attributes (React's `DOMAttributes#onClick`); one declared by another package's type is that library component's prop, one declared by a type of the project is the project component's. In `noir_kinds`, the entry kind of each `kind` Noir gives an endpoint that Daodan knows (a server action is no entry): the endpoint then takes that `kind` as its shape, and any other `kind` changes nothing. In `components`, by grammar, the query that reads the decorators of a file and its named imports from its tree (`entry_points/angular.py`): @decorator with its @name and @arguments, and @imported with its @local alias and its @module; the reader keeps the decorators whose name is what the `decorator` of the module `module` is imported as, and reads its properties `template` and `url`: the names a framework's component is written with. In `nitro_routes`, by grammar, the query that reads the file Nitro writes for a Nuxt project (`nuxt prepare`: `.nuxt/types/nitro-routes.d.ts`, `entry_points/nuxt.py`), whose `InternalApi` interface ties each server route to its HTTP methods and each method to the import of its handler's file: @route and @methods, the route and the object type of its methods; @method and @value, a method and its type (the key `default` is a handler with no method in its file name); @import, any import of a file in a type, which `entries.nitro_routes` assigns to the method and the route that contain it, whatever the generics around it. In `nuxt` (`entry_points/nuxt.py`), by shape: a `server-route` is one of those routes, whose `exports` start a flow, the `default` export that Nitro calls; a `page` is a route Nuxt resolves from a page of the app (`loadNuxt` and the hook `pages:resolved`, run by `entry_points/nuxt_pages.mjs`), a row on the page's file with no `exports`, as the file is the entry.
